title: Week 10 - Sorting Algorithms I
description: Practice comparison, swapping, selection sort, bubble sort, and swap-count statistics.

questions.title: Swap Two Adjacent Height Values That Are Out of Order
questions.description:
## Difficulty

Simple

## Background

A line of students' heights is stored in the array heights. The teacher notices that the student at position index and the student at position index + 1 may be out of order. If the first is taller than the second, they need to be swapped.

## Task

Check two adjacent heights and swap them if their order is wrong.

## Input

One array heights and one number index.

## Output

Return the processed heights array.

## Hint

Only two adjacent positions need to be compared.
questions.reference_code:
function solution(heights, index)
    if heights[index] > heights[index + 1] then
        local temp = heights[index]
        heights[index] = heights[index + 1]
        heights[index + 1] = temp
    end

    return heights
end

questions.title: Find the Position of the Minimum Value in a Score List
questions.description:
## Difficulty

Simple

## Background

The first step of selection sort usually needs to find the position of the minimum value in a group of data.

## Task

Find the position of the minimum score in the scores array.

## Input

One array scores and one number n.

## Output

Return the position of the minimum value.

## Hint

You can first assume the first position is the minimum, then compare each item.
questions.reference_code:
function solution(scores, n)
    local minIndex = 1

    for i = 2, n do
        if scores[i] < scores[minIndex] then
            minIndex = i
        end
    end

    return minIndex
end

questions.title: Complete the First Round of Selection Sort
questions.description:
## Difficulty

Simple

## Background

Each round of selection sort finds the smallest value in the remaining data and puts it at the current front position.

## Task

Complete the first round of selection sort by swapping the minimum value into position 1.

## Input

One array numbers and one number n.

## Output

Return the numbers array after the first round.

## Hint

Find the minimum position first, then swap it with the first position.
questions.reference_code:
function solution(numbers, n)
    local minIndex = 1

    for i = 2, n do
        if numbers[i] < numbers[minIndex] then
            minIndex = i
        end
    end

    local temp = numbers[1]
    numbers[1] = numbers[minIndex]
    numbers[minIndex] = temp

    return numbers
end

questions.title: Use Selection Sort to Organize a Game Score Ranking
questions.description:
## Difficulty

Normal

## Background

Game scores are stored in the array scores. The system needs to arrange the scores from low to high so it is easy to view the ranking from bottom to top.

## Task

Use selection sort to sort scores from small to large.

## Input

One array scores and one number n.

## Output

Return the sorted scores array.

## Hint

In each round, put the smallest value from the remaining data at the current front position.
questions.reference_code:
function solution(scores, n)
    for i = 1, n - 1 do
        local minIndex = i

        for j = i + 1, n do
            if scores[j] < scores[minIndex] then
                minIndex = j
            end
        end

        local temp = scores[i]
        scores[i] = scores[minIndex]
        scores[minIndex] = temp
    end

    return scores
end

questions.title: Use Selection Sort to Sort Book Numbers from Small to Large
questions.description:
## Difficulty

Normal

## Background

The library receives a batch of new books, and the book numbers are out of order. The administrator needs to arrange the book numbers from small to large.

## Task

Use selection sort to organize the books array.

## Input

One array books and one number n.

## Output

Return the books array sorted from small to large.

## Hint

The sorting process needs to find the smallest number in the current range many times.
questions.reference_code:
function solution(books, n)
    for i = 1, n - 1 do
        local minIndex = i

        for j = i + 1, n do
            if books[j] < books[minIndex] then
                minIndex = j
            end
        end

        local temp = books[i]
        books[i] = books[minIndex]
        books[minIndex] = temp
    end

    return books
end

questions.title: Complete One Left-to-Right Pass of Bubble Sort
questions.description:
## Difficulty

Normal

## Background

Bubble sort repeatedly compares adjacent data and swaps them if their order is wrong. After one pass, larger data moves toward the back.

## Task

Complete one left-to-right bubble pass on numbers and count the swaps in this pass.

## Input

One array numbers and one number n.

## Output

Return the processed numbers array and the swap count in order.

## Hint

Do only one pass of adjacent comparisons; full sorting is not needed.
questions.reference_code:
function solution(numbers, n)
    local swaps = 0

    for i = 1, n - 1 do
        if numbers[i] > numbers[i + 1] then
            local temp = numbers[i]
            numbers[i] = numbers[i + 1]
            numbers[i + 1] = temp
            swaps = swaps + 1
        end
    end

    return numbers, swaps
end

questions.title: Use Bubble Sort to Arrange Scores from High to Low
questions.description:
## Difficulty

Challenge

## Background

Competition scores are stored in the array scores. The leaderboard needs to show scores from high to low.

## Task

Use bubble sort to sort scores from large to small.

## Input

One array scores and one number n.

## Output

Return the scores array sorted from high to low.

## Hint

When comparing adjacent values, the larger score should move toward the front.
questions.reference_code:
function solution(scores, n)
    for i = 1, n - 1 do
        for j = 1, n - i do
            if scores[j] < scores[j + 1] then
                local temp = scores[j]
                scores[j] = scores[j + 1]
                scores[j + 1] = temp
            end
        end
    end

    return scores
end

questions.title: Count Swaps When Bubble Sorting a Seat Table
questions.description:
## Difficulty

Challenge

## Background

Seat numbers are stored in the array seats. The teacher wants to use bubble sort to arrange the numbers from small to large and also wants to know how many seat swaps happen.

## Task

Use bubble sort to organize seats and count the total number of swaps.

## Input

One array seats and one number n.

## Output

Return the sorted seats array and the swap count in order.

## Hint

Increase the swap count only when an adjacent swap actually happens.
questions.reference_code:
function solution(seats, n)
    local swaps = 0

    for i = 1, n - 1 do
        for j = 1, n - i do
            if seats[j] > seats[j + 1] then
                local temp = seats[j]
                seats[j] = seats[j + 1]
                seats[j + 1] = temp
                swaps = swaps + 1
            end
        end
    end

    return seats, swaps
end

questions.title: Compare Selection Sort and Bubble Sort Swap Counts on the Same Data
questions.description:
## Difficulty

Challenge

## Background

The same data can be organized with selection sort or bubble sort. The teacher wants to compare how many swaps the two sorting methods make on the same data.

## Task

Copy the original array, sort one copy with selection sort and one copy with bubble sort from small to large, then return the two swap counts.

## Input

One array numbers and one number n.

## Output

Return the selection-sort swap count and bubble-sort swap count in order.

## Hint

The two sorts need to operate on their own arrays so they do not affect each other.
questions.reference_code:
function solution(numbers, n)
    local a = {}
    local b = {}

    for i = 1, n do
        a[i] = numbers[i]
        b[i] = numbers[i]
    end

    local selectionSwaps = 0
    for i = 1, n - 1 do
        local minIndex = i
        for j = i + 1, n do
            if a[j] < a[minIndex] then
                minIndex = j
            end
        end

        if minIndex ~= i then
            local temp = a[i]
            a[i] = a[minIndex]
            a[minIndex] = temp
            selectionSwaps = selectionSwaps + 1
        end
    end

    local bubbleSwaps = 0
    for i = 1, n - 1 do
        for j = 1, n - i do
            if b[j] > b[j + 1] then
                local temp = b[j]
                b[j] = b[j + 1]
                b[j + 1] = temp
                bubbleSwaps = bubbleSwaps + 1
            end
        end
    end

    return selectionSwaps, bubbleSwaps
end
